name: KOI-KOI
description: Koi-Koi is the most popular card game played with traditional Japanese 'Hanafuda' (Flower Cards). Played between two people, it is a fishing (capture) game where players aim to form specific combinations of cards called 'Yaku'. The name 'Koi-Koi' refers to the strategic choice a player makes after forming a Yaku: either to end the round and take their points, or to call 'Koi-Koi' (Come On!) to continue play in hopes of a higher score at the risk of losing it all.

content.text: Koi-Koi is the most popular card game played with traditional Japanese 'Hanafuda' (Flower Cards). Played between two people, it is a fishing (capture) game where players aim to form specific combinations of cards called 'Yaku'. The name 'Koi-Koi' refers to the strategic choice a player makes after forming a Yaku: either to end the round and take their points, or to call 'Koi-Koi' (Come On!) to continue play in hopes of a higher score at the risk of losing it all.
Originates from 18th-century Japan. Hanafuda cards were developed as a way to circumvent government bans on Western-style gambling cards, using floral imagery instead of numbers.
48 cards. Suits by month: January (Pine), February (Plum), March (Cherry)... to December (Paulownia). Each suit has 4 cards of varying value (Bright, Animal, Ribbon, Chaff).

Each player is dealt 8 cards face-down; 8 cards are placed face-up in the 'field' (ba). The rest form the draw pile.

items.text: 6 rounds: Play 6 hands instead of 12; players may agree before the game.
Koi-Koi once per hand: Player may call Koi-Koi only once per hand (not on every yaku-forming turn).
Tsukimi-zake and Hanami-zake optional: Some rulesets omit the Moon Viewing and Flower Viewing yaku.
Ino-Shika-Cho Yaku: The boar, deer, and butterfly scoring combination in Koi-Koi; kept as Koi-Koi rules content rather than a separate game.
